themes.title: Coverage and copay are unclear until late in the booking
themes.description: Participants wanted to know up front whether a provider takes their insurance and what the visit would cost, and left the app to check their insurer's portal.
themes.opportunity: Show in-network status and an estimated copay on each provider card.
themes.effortNote: Requires an insurance eligibility integration and copay estimates.

quotes.text: I wanted to know if she's in-network. I had to leave the app and dig through my insurance portal to find out if I'm covered.
The insurance thing is confusing. It lists accepted plans but doesn't say what my copay would be.
I couldn't tell if my insurance was covered until the confirmation screen.

themes.title: Reminders help participants feel prepared
themes.description: Participants said the text reminder before the visit made them confident they would not forget it.
themes.opportunity: Extend reminders with directions and a preparation checklist.
themes.effortNote: Extends the existing reminder messages with extra content.

quotes.text: The text message reminder the day before was great. It gave me a heads up and I didn't forget.
I got a reminder and a text message with directions, which was handy.
The reminder was nice. A heads up the morning of was perfect.

themes.title: Finding open appointment times across providers takes too many steps
themes.description: Participants could not tell who was free this week from the results list and had to open each provider's profile one at a time to look for an opening.
themes.opportunity: Show open times for each provider in search results, with a combined calendar view.
themes.effortNote: Needs a combined availability feed across providers and a calendar view in search.

quotes.text: Honestly I open the app and try to see who's available this week, but I can't tell from the list. There's no calendar until you click into each doctor.
Open slots matter most to me. I work shifts, so I need a calendar view across all providers, not one at a time.
No slots showed until I tapped each name. The availability is hidden.

themes.title: Moving an appointment means calling the clinic
themes.description: Participants could not reschedule or cancel in the app and had to phone the clinic during office hours.
themes.opportunity: Add self-serve reschedule and cancel with clear change windows.
themes.effortNote: Self-serve changes need clinic scheduling rules and notifications.

quotes.text: Later I needed to reschedule and the only option was to call the office. I was on hold for ten minutes.
To cancel I had to call the office during business hours. Why can't I cancel in the app?
I had to reschedule by phone. Nobody picked up so I left a voicemail.

themes.title: The booking form asks for information the app already has
themes.description: Participants entered details they had already given, such as name and contact information, and found the form repetitive.
themes.opportunity: Prefill the form from the profile and remember family members.
themes.effortNote: Prefilling from the profile touches the form and account data.

quotes.text: Then the form. It asked for my address and date of birth, then asked for the same information again on the next screen. Too many steps for a checkup.
I re-enter my details every time I book for my kids. It's tedious.
There are so many fields. The long form made me nearly give up.

themes.title: Fees appear late and the total is higher than the listing
themes.description: Participants were surprised at confirmation by a total above the price they had seen on the listing.
themes.opportunity: Include every fee in the first listed price.
themes.effortNote: Pricing must include fees from the first listing, which affects backend and display.

quotes.text: At the end there was an extra fee I hadn't seen. I was surprised, the total cost was thirty dollars higher than the listing.
The price was a surprise at checkout. There was a booking fee that wasn't mentioned earlier.

themes.title: Follow-up instructions are easy to lose
themes.description: Participants said instructions given after the visit were hard to find later.
themes.opportunity: Keep the visit summary and follow-up plan in the app.
themes.effortNote: Needs a visit summary object and a place to show it in the app.

quotes.text: After the visit I lost the instructions. There's no visit summary in the app.
Nothing arrived after the visit. I'd want notes from the doctor and the follow-up plan in one place.

themes.title: Ratings and recommendations decide who participants consider
themes.description: Participants screen providers on star ratings and on whether friends recommend them before they look at availability.
themes.opportunity: Keep ratings prominent in results and make recommendations visible.
themes.effortNote: Ratings already exist; mostly a layout change.

quotes.text: I always check reviews first. If somebody has a rating under four I skip them, and I like when friends recommend someone.
I read the reviews, and the recommended badge made me pick her.

themes.title: Participants want to know what to bring or prepare
themes.description: Participants asked what paperwork or steps they needed before arriving, and some made a second trip.
themes.opportunity: Send a visit-specific checklist after booking.
themes.effortNote: A static checklist sent after booking.

quotes.text: I wasn't sure what to bring, so I just arrived with my ID. A list of paperwork would help me prepare.
I'd like to know what to bring and if I need to arrive early to fill forms before.
